steps.say: Stress urinary incontinence is leakage on effort such as coughing. Urethral hypermobility is caused by lost pelvic support. Intrinsic sphincter deficiency is defined by low leak pressures. ALPP under 60 cmH2O is considered diagnostic. MUCP under 20 cmH2O is added confirmation. Mixed urgency is assessed alongside stress symptoms.
steps.tx: **Stress urinary incontinence** (leak on coughing, SUI (effort leakage)) comes from urethral hypermobility (loose pelvic support) or **intrinsic sphincter deficiency** (weak closure, ISD (worn valve)) defined by **ALPP** (leak pressure test) under **60 cmH2O** (sixty) with MUCP under **20 cmH2O** (twenty). Test with cough stress and urodynamics together, because mixed urgency often hides beside the stress leak.

steps.say: Midurethral slings are offered for hypermobile stress incontinence. Retropubic TVT is passed over the pubic bone. Transobturator TOT is passed through the obturator foramina. Tension free placement is performed under the mid urethra. Fibrosis is relied upon for lasting anchorage. Obstructive tightness is avoided carefully during cough testing.
steps.tx: **Midurethral sling** (tape under the mid urethra) operations, retropubic **TVT** (over the top tape) and transobturator **TOT** (side to side tape), are the standard for hypermobile female stress incontinence. Place the tape tension free at the mid urethra and let fibrosis anchor it, because continence needs support, not tightness.

vis.alt: Management ladder for stress incontinence with a midurethral polypropylene mesh sling at the mid urethra as surgical gold standard.
vis.caption: Midurethral sling is the surgical gold standard for hypermobile stress incontinence: tension free tape at the mid urethra. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.say: Autologous fascial sling is selected for complicated cases. Recurrent incontinence is treated after failed tapes. Severe sphincter deficiency is corrected with living tissue. Mesh erosion and diverticulum are repaired at the same time. Rectus fascia is harvested through a low cut. Fixation is performed at the endopelvic fascia.
steps.tx: **Autologous fascial sling** (patient's own tissue hammock), the rectus fascia **pubovaginal sling** (belly wall strip), rescues complicated, recurrent, or severely deficient sphincters and repairs mesh erosion or diverticulum. Harvest rectus fascia through a low transverse cut and fix it at the endopelvic fascia, because living tissue integrates where mesh failed.

steps.say: Overactive bladder is managed by a stepped ladder. Behavioural therapy is tried carefully before any drugs. Antimuscarinics are prescribed as second line agents. Solifenacin and oxybutynin are used widely as first choices. Mirabegron 50 mg is offered as a beta-3 agonist. Dry mouth is expected and managed proactively with fluids.
steps.tx: **Overactive bladder** (urgent frequent bladder, OAB (rushed bladder)) climbs a ladder: behaviour first, then **antimuscarinics** (bladder calmants) like solifenacin and oxybutynin, or **beta-3 agonist** (new relaxant) **mirabegron** 50 mg and vibegron 75 mg. Warn about dry mouth and constipation with antimuscarinics, because M3 blockade dries every gland.

vis.alt: Bladder detrusor with M3 blockade relaxing smooth muscle.
vis.caption: M3 blockade calms the overactive detrusor: watch for dry mouth. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.say: Third line therapy is offered for refractory overactivity. OnabotulinumtoxinA 100 units is injected into the detrusor. Sacral neuromodulation is implanted as a bladder pacemaker. PTNS is delivered gently through the ankle weekly. Repeat injections are scheduled every six to nine months. Residual volumes are checked after each treatment.
steps.tx: Refractory overactivity moves to third line: bladder wall **onabotulinumtoxinA** (Botox bladder injections) **100 units** (one hundred), sacral neuromodulation (bladder pacemaker, InterStim (implanted pulse generator)), or tibial nerve tingling (PTNS (ankle stimulation)). Repeat Botox every six to nine months and check residuals, because retention follows overtreatment.

steps.say: Artificial urinary sphincter is implanted for severe male leakage. Post-prostatectomy incontinence is the classic indication. The AMS 800 device is assembled from cuff pump and balloon. Cycling is taught before hospital discharge. Night deactivation is advised for high risk urethras.
steps.tx: The **artificial urinary sphincter** (implanted squeeze cuff, **AUS** (AMS 800)) is the gold standard for severe male **post-prostatectomy incontinence** (leak after prostate removal) from sphincter failure. It cycles cuff pressure with a scrotal pump, so teach cycling before discharge, because an always closed cuff erodes.

steps.say: Male slings are offered for mild to moderate leakage. One to 3 pads daily is the usual range. A working sphincter remnant is required for success. No pump handling is needed afterwards by the patient. AUS is reserved for severe total incontinence. Patient dexterity is assessed carefully before device selection.
steps.tx: **Male slings** (hammock under the urethra), including transobturator and adjustable quadratic designs, suit mild to moderate leaks of **1 to 3 pads** (one to three) daily with a working sphincter remnant, called a **post-prostatectomy sling** (male support tape) after prostatectomy. Prefer them over AUS when pads stay few, because slings need no pump handling.

steps.say: Burch colposuspension is performed openly for anatomical hypermobility. The endopelvic fascia is stitched to Cooper ligament. Open or laparoscopic access is used for fixation. No synthetic mesh is implanted during the repair. Women refusing tapes are counselled for this option. Erosion risk is avoided entirely with native tissue.
steps.tx: **Burch colposuspension** (vaginal wall lift) stitches the paravaginal endopelvic fascia to **Cooper ligament** (Cooper's iliopectineal line) through open or laparoscopic access for anatomical hypermobility. It skips mesh entirely, so offer it to women who refuse synthetic tapes, because native tissue repair avoids erosion risk.
